verses.1: And after being rescued at that time, we learned that the island is called Melite.
verses.2: And those barbarians also did not take advantage of our kind-hearted actions. They set fire to everything we had, because of the evil intentions they harbored.
verses.3: When Paul’s clothes were caught in the flames, a large amount of heat was generated. This heat caused his hand to burn off.
verses.4: And when the barbarians saw how they were carrying away the monster from its hands, they said to each other: “Surely this man is a murderer. He who was rescued from the sea didn’t deserve to live after suffering such punishment.”
verses.5: So, you should throw that monster into the fire. It doesn’t do any harm at all.
verses.6: But those who foresaw that he would soon die or be killed in an instant, thought nothing strange about this. Instead of thinking anything unusual about his situation, they began to call him a god.
verses.7: And near that place, there was a region called Poplyo. They, three of us, were brutally exploited by them for three days.
verses.8: And the father of Popilius was continuously suffering from fever and other illnesses. When Paul went to see him, he took his hands in his own and comforted him.
verses.9: And because of this, the others who lived on the island also became ill and were treated accordingly.
verses.10: They also honored us greatly, and they took care of all our needs.
verses.11: After three months, we arrived at the island of Alexandretta, along with the ships belonging to the Dioskuros family.
verses.12: And after entering Syraksas, we stayed there for three days.
verses.13: From there, we continued our journey towards Rhygon. After a day, during the night, we arrived at Potiolus.
verses.14: After finding our brothers, we were ordered to stay with them for seven days. And in this way, we arrived at the Temple of Jerusalem.
verses.15: From there, the brothers, having heard about us, came to meet us up to Appius Forus and Trion Tavernus. When Paul saw them, he thanked God, and then he continued his journey.
verses.16: And when we entered Jerusalem, Paul was ordered to stay there with the soldier who was in charge of him.
verses.17: After three days, he gathered together the leading men of the Jews. When they came together, he said to them, “Men, brothers, I have been brought out of Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans, without doing anything against the people or their laws. I am now in their hands.”
verses.18: In order to discredit me, they wanted to claim that there was no reason for my death.
verses.19: However, since the Jews were speaking against me, I was forced to call upon Caesars for help. But he didn’t have any right to accuse me as belonging to my own people.
verses.20: Therefore, I have called upon you to come and see this, so that I can fulfill the hopes of Israel.
verses.21: But those who spoke to him said, “We have not received any letters about you from Judea. Nor has anyone among our brothers told us anything bad about you.”
verses.22: But it is worthy of our hearing what you intend to do. After all, since we know what this decision involves, it’s clear that it goes against all principles.
verses.23: And those who traveled with him that day, they came to him in order to hear his teachings. He then admonished them about the kingdom of God, convincing them to follow Jesus, according to the laws of Moses and the prophets, from morning till evening.
verses.24: And those who were persuaded believed in what was said; but those who did not believe, they remained unconvinced.
verses.25: Being disagreeing with each other, they continued to argue. When Paul asked them what the meaning of this was, they said that it meant that the holy Spirit had spoken through Isaiah to your fathers.
verses.26: And he said, “Go to the people and say this: ‘Listen carefully, and do not forget to listen. And when you see something, do not ignore it.’”
verses.27: For the hearts of this people have become sharp and perceptive. They can hear loudly, and their ears are sensitive. If they see those who speak loudly, they will listen carefully, with their hearts also joining in. Then I will be able to understand them.
verses.28: It is known to you that this salvation of God has been sent to the nations. They will also hear about it.
verses.30: He received an entire year’s salary in one lump sum. He also accepted everyone who came to seek his help.
verses.31: He proclaimed the kingdom of God and taught about the Lord Jesus Christ with complete dedication.
